detail.body:
## Purpose

Move kernel block splitting from the block table into each attention group. Previously `BlockTable` split every manager block for the whole KV cache group (`kernel_block_sizes`). All backends in a group had to share one kernel block size, block tables and slot mappings were at kernel granularity, and packed (block-outermost) caches could not be split at all, since other layers' pages sit between a layer's blocks. Now block tables stay at manager granularity, and each `AttentionGroup` maps manager blocks to the kernel blocks its own backend needs.

On top of this, GLM-5.3-Flash moves to the generic packed KV layout, and its model-specific KV code is removed.

## Design

### Kernel block mapping

**Choosing the kernel block size**
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` picks a size per KV cache group with `select_common_block_size(manager, backends, specs)`. Packed groups keep the manager block size and are never split group-wide.
- Each `AttentionGroup` then picks its own size for its backend and spec. It sets `kernel_block_size` only when that is smaller than the manager block.

**Mapping block tables**
- The group maps manager block `b` to kernel blocks `b * stride + j` (`j < block_size / kernel_block_size`).
  - `stride` is the number of kernel blocks per manager block.
  - For packed caches it is the packed block stride in kernel blocks.
- The mapped table is persistent and preallocated per ubatch, so CUDA graphs capture a stable buffer.
- Mapping happens inside `build_metadata`, `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` and `build_metadata_for_drafting`. All runners and drafters (V1/MRv2, EAGLE, Gemma4, Step3.5, DFlash) go through these. Fused multi-step draft decode re-maps before replaying a FULL graph.
- `BlockTable`/`InputBatch` (V1 and MRv2) drop `kernel_block_sizes`. Slot mappings, CP and DFlash stay at manager granularity.

**Mapping KV views**
- When KV caches are bound, each group views its cache in kernel blocks. Packed caches use `as_strided` with the packed block stride.
- Only compressed caches (`tokens_per_state > 1`) may be split this way, because their write slots come from the mapped block table. Token and pooled caches are written through manager-block slot mappings, so they are rejected.
- The KV block zeroer maps the views back to manager blocks.

**Alignment**
- `block_stride_alignment` accepts `MultipleOf(n)`, meaning whole kernel blocks of up to `n` tokens, so a packed block always splits into whole kernel blocks.
- Fixed-size backends get it automatically; sparse MLA backends set their own in `customize_spec`.
- Bytes per block: block-outermost layouts round to the lcm of all alignments; layer-outermost layouts pad each layer's page separately.

**Consumers:** NIXL, Mooncake and HiSparse pick kernel block sizes the same way as the worker.

### GLM-5.3-Flash

- Uses the packed `BLHNC` layout. Removed its custom groups, byte layout, `KpoolTailSpec` and `storage_block_size`.
- The kpool indexer is a compressed spec whose backend declares DeepGEMM page sizes (32/64; 64 on SM120). The tail is a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of `kpool + num_speculative_tokens`.
- FlashMLA fp8 on SM90 reads 64-token pages over flat rows, so packed blocks need not be split.

**Example** (GLM-5.3-Flash on H200, manager block = 640 tokens, `index_kpool = 4`):

| Attention group | States per manager block | Kernel block | Kernel blocks per manager block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sparse MLA (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`) | 640 | 640 (no split) | 1 |
| kpool indexer (`tokens_per_state = 4`) | 160 | 32 (DeepGEMM page) | 5 |

For a request with manager block table `[7, 2]`:
- **Sparse MLA** builds its metadata from `[7, 2]` unchanged.
- **The indexer group** maps it to `[7·S, …, 7·S+4, 2·S, …, 2·S+4]`, where `S` is the stride between manager blocks in kernel blocks:
  - In a plain (layer-outermost) cache, `S = 5`, giving `[35..39, 10..14]`.
  - In the packed `BLHNC` cache, each manager block also holds the other layers' pages, so `S` is the packed block size divided by the indexer's 32-state page. `MultipleOf` alignment keeps that an integer.

The scheduler, slot mappings and other groups never see kernel blocks. On main, the whole group had to share one kernel block size, so the indexer needed the GLM-only `storage_block_size` workaround instead.

## Test Result

Each cell is GSM8K / GPQA Diamond / acceptance length; no request errors.

| Platform | Model / backend | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | GLM `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, MTP5 | 0.9280 / 0.7323 / 4.73 | 0.9333 / 0.7374 / 4.73 |
| GB200 | DSv4.1 default, DSpark5 | 0.9257 / 0.8384 / 4.08 | 0.9261 / 0.8460 / 4.01 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` | — | 0.9386 / 0.7323 / 4.78 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + `fp8_ds_mla` (GSM8K / accept) | 0.9325 / 3.937 | 0.9348 / 3.930 |
| H200 | DSv4.1 default | — | 0.9272 / 0.8535 / 4.05 |
| MI350X | GLM `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` | 0.9211 / 0.6768 / 3.33 | 0.9191 / 0.6835 / 4.82 |
| MI350X | DSv4.1 default | 0.9272 / 0.8333 / 4.03 | 0.9303 / 0.8535 / 3.94 |

- **Prefix caching:** mid-block hits give byte-identical outputs to main.
- **NIXL 1P1D:** GLM 0.9401, DSv4.1 0.9265, 0 failed transfers.
- **Mooncake P/D:** GLM 0.9136.

Performance, PR vs main (medians, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64):

| Platform | Model / workload | Output throughput | TTFT p50 | TPOT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | GLM 4K/1K | −0.1% / +3.5% / +0.3% | −3.4% / −4.6% / +0.7% | −1.9% / +0.7% / −1.5% |
| GB200 | GLM 32K/1K | +0.0% / +1.8% / +0.5% | −0.3% / −0.1% / −1.9% | −0.8% / −5.7% / −2.0% |
| GB200 | GLM sonnet | +4.3% / +0.7% / +0.2% | −21.2% / +0.5% / −24.8% | +2.2% / −0.1% / −1.4% |
| GB200 | DSv4.1 4K/1K | −0.1% / −1.4% / +1.7% | +0.0% / +0.3% / +0.3% | −7.0% / +0.6% / −1.4% |
| H200 | GLM 4K/1K | +6.0% / +2.4% / +1.6% | +0.2% / −3.0% / −0.3% | −3.3% / +2.0% / −3.5% |
| H200 | GLM sonnet | +11.2% / −1.6% / +1.2% | −3.6% / −2.4% / −1.5% | −2.0% / +6.4% / −0.6% |
| H200 | DSv4.1 4K/1K | +6.2% / +1.9% / +0.5% | +6.0% / −3.6% / +0.2% | −14.6% / −1.3% / −0.5% |
| MI350X | GLM 4K/1K (random) | −8.6% / −9.9% / −9.2% | +0.3% / −0.2% / −0.5% | +7.8% / +3.3% / +4.3% |
| MI350X | GLM sonnet | +3.3% / +8.8% / +8.7% | +2.5% / +0.2% / +2.7% | −4.3% / −7.9% / −7.6% |
| MI350X | DSv4.1 4K/1K | +1.3% / −3.2% / −0.3% | −2.9% / −4.7% / −0.9% | +1.7% / +4.8% / −0.4% |

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed and validated by the author.

+"""GLM-5.3-Flash indexer kernel block sizes are DeepGEMM pool pages."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla import indexer

+
+KPOOL = 4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "rocm,sm120,expected",
+    [
+        (False, False, [KPOOL * 32, KPOOL * 64]),
+        # SM120 DeepGEMM takes only 64-entry pages for the fp8 cache.
+        (False, True, [KPOOL * 64]),
+        # ROCm's AITER paged-MQA logits take the same pool pages.
+        (True, False, [KPOOL * 32, KPOOL * 64]),
+    ],
+)
+def test_glm5next_indexer_kernel_block_sizes(monkeypatch, rocm, sm120, expected):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(current_platform, "is_rocm", lambda: rocm)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(

+        "is_device_capability_family",
+        lambda family: sm120 and family == 120,
+    )
+    model_config = SimpleNamespace(hf_text_config=SimpleNamespace(index_kpool=KPOOL))
+    config = SimpleNamespace(model_config=model_config)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(indexer, "get_current_vllm_config", lambda: config)
+
+    spec = SimpleNamespace(tokens_per_state=KPOOL)
+    assert Glm5NextIndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes(spec) == expected
+    # Platform block-size selection queries without a spec.
+    assert Glm5NextIndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes() == expected

In layer-outermost layouts `bytes_per_block` isn't a stride (each layer's pages are packed densely), so rounding the sum to the lcm of alignments aligns nothing and just lowers `num_blocks`. With every fixed-size backend now getting `MultipleOf`, that's ~11% fewer blocks for DSV3.2 at block size 128 (MLA + indexer pages: 6,152,704 -> 6,927,360 B/block), while integer alignments a page doesn't meet are silently missed.

Suggestion: align where the stride actually is, e.g.

```python
def _get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block(
    kv_cache_groups: list[KVCacheGroupSpec], layout: KVCacheLayout
) -> int:
    """Return the largest cache group's bytes per block."""
    group_specs = [
        [_get_per_layer_spec(group, name) for name in group.layer_names]
        for group in kv_cache_groups
    ]
    if layout.is_block_outermost:
        # One block stride spans every group's pages.
        alignment = math.lcm(
            *(
                group.kv_cache_spec.page_size_bytes
                for group in kv_cache_groups
                if isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, HiSparseHotSpec)
            ),
            *(s.get_block_stride_alignment() for specs in group_specs for s in specs),
        )
        block_strides = lambda specs: [
            round_up(sum(s.page_size_bytes for s in specs), alignment)
        ]
    else:
        # Each layer's block stride is its own page.
        block_strides = lambda specs: [
            round_up(s.page_size_bytes, s.get_block_stride_alignment()) for s in specs
        ]
    bytes_per_block = max(sum(block_strides(specs)) for specs in group_specs)
    assert bytes_per_block > 0
    return bytes_per_block
```

(with the layer-outer path in `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` using the padded page as its block stride). `MultipleOf` is then free there, since `page(bs)` is already a multiple of `page(kernel_bs)`.

I didn't fully understand the fused path before.. I went back through the related codes, mainly in #58463.

The issue only happens in **fused** draft decode + **FULL cudagraph**. In that mode the speculator replays the captured graph without calling `build()`. So only the manager block table gets updated each step. The kernel block table is never re-mapped, so it stays stale. My guard here is truly too broad. Here are two ways to fix:
- remap inside the captured refresh. This follows #58463's idea: add in `update_draft_decode_metadata`: maps the current block table into its kernel block table. The cost is that the group keeps a reference to the block table view it maps from.
- map outside the graph before each fused FULL replay. Simpler and no extra state, but it adds an eager map outside the graph, which kind of against #58463.

I prefer the first method. What do you think?

## Update

Thanks so much @LucasWilkinson  for the suggestion in https://github.com/andakai/vllm/pull/7 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59297! This PR now follows. I agree the design is cleaner. Welcome more comments about the pr. cc @ivanium @simon-veitner-redhat @simondanielsson @JaredforReal 

- The original version stored block tables in kernel blocks and had metadata builders re-page the indexer tables. 
- Now block tables and slot mappings stay in manager blocks everywhere. Only an `AttentionGroup` whose backend needs smaller blocks maps its table at metadata build time, and only the packed kpool indexer gets a re-strided view. `BlockTable` and the builders no longer know about kernel blocks, so the design is much simpler.

## follow-up changes

Fixes:
- V1 runner: keeps scheduler-block KV views, so prefix-cache CoW works on split packed layers (`87cfe3477d`).
- V2 MTP draft groups: now also map kernel blocks; draft decode previously read the wrong indexer pages (`a8c99be31f`).
- DSv4.1 replay groups: no longer share the target groups' mapped block table (`f5fa0ee479`).
- ROCm GLM-5.3 indexer: keeps DeepGEMM pool pages, which fixes the AITER paged-MQA assert on MI350X (`636d1f842e`).
- do some unused codes cleanups

## Validation

**setups**

PR `636d1f842e` vs main `84bcbc6264`.
- Hardware: GB200 TP4, H200 TP8, MI350X TP8.
- GLM-5.3-Flash: BF16 KV with MTP (5 speculative tokens).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: DSpark (5 speculative tokens).
- Evals: full GSM8K (1319) and GPQA Diamond (198) at temperature 0.

**Accuracy**

| Platform | Model | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 (2-run mean) | GLM | 0.9280 / 0.7323 / 4.73 | 0.9333 / 0.7374 / 4.73 |

commit ef4fb8f0f1 update after merging origin/main:

FlashMLA + fp8 on SM90: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59246 lets GLM-5.3 use an fp8 kvcache on hopper.
